hook.line: Your video isn't ranking anywhere, so let's talk about the secret TikTok setting that's killing your SEO.
hook.visual: Creator talking to camera at a laptop, a reply-to-comment bubble top left and a white 'SEO hack for beginners Part2' title box mid-frame, with small word-by-word captions low in the frame.

beats.what: Reply-to-comment sticker plus 'Part2' title box frame it as a series follow-up; she names the problem (videos not ranking).
First cut: 'welcome to class' resets into the lesson; recaps that hashtags are dead and keywords must be spoken.
A big yellow handwritten '5' pops over her face as she says 'first five seconds'.
She announces one more step before posting; the script-font Edit Cover word follows as she names the hidden setting.
Cut to a phone screen recording of TikTok's edit-cover text tool showing where to type the keyword.
Back to her face; second tip: add four or five keywords at the end of the caption ('Caption' pop word).
Worked example: a CapCut tutorial, with 'Capcut Tutorial' script text over her.
Payoff line: TikTok is a database, not a video app ('Algorithm' pop word).
'Assignment' pop word: she restates both steps as homework for the next post.
CTA: comment 'SEO part three' for more keyword tricks.

why_it_works: Reply-to-comment bubble plus 'Part 2' title makes it feel like the answer to a real viewer's question and promises a series, so returning viewers stay.
Single keyword pops (5, Edit Cover, Caption, Algorithm, Assignment) land on the exact spoken word, giving the eye a new hit every 10-20 s in a long single-shot talk.
The one screen recording of the edit-cover text tool shows the hidden setting instead of describing it, at the moment of the reveal.
Comment-keyword CTA ('SEO part three') turns the next episode into a comment request, which feeds engagement.
weaknesses: Only 2.52 cuts per minute and a 64.8 s longest shot: the middle stretch about caption keywords is one unbroken take.
75% of text sits outside the safe area, so the title box and captions risk being covered by TikTok's UI.
The worked example (CapCut keywords) is spoken only; no screen shows the caption being typed.
for_robert: Copy the single-word pop on the key spoken term (one stylised word per idea, timed to the word); Fred could carry or point at that word as it lands instead of it just appearing.
